summary:
I've been running a local inference box with one 16 GB GPU that a handful of services share: the brain behind my agent, image generation in ComfyUI, and a couple of roleplay models. Switchboard is the proxy that keeps them from evicting each other. The bug I liked most this month: ComfyUI renders hold the GPU through a lease. When I tested it by holding a lease under a different client name, Switchboard evicted ComfyUI itself. ComfyUI's coordinator then blocked inside its own event loop, and the whole server went dark until the lease timed out. I also switched the MoE models to load fully into RAM instead of memory-mapping, because experts were paging off disk mid-token. Cold generation went from 4.6 to 32 tokens per second.

The box also got a power log. The original cron entry vanished without a word on one date and left a 15-day hole that I noticed two weeks later. It's a systemd timer now, and the dashboard banner goes red when samples stop. Unlocking real CPU readings showed idle draw around 30 W, not the 95 W my model had assumed, so the estimate has a discontinuity on that date. Four months of data put the mean at about 179 W, roughly 131 kWh a month. I added the same counters to internal fleet-monitoring tooling, and that box turns out to be about 85% of the fleet's measurable draw.

Most of my project time went into a tabletop-RPG companion app I'm building. The bug worth telling: about ten components each opened their own realtime channel for one campaign, but the client library hands back the same channel per topic. The second caller threw an error, and closing any panel silently killed dice and presence for the rest of the page. It's now one ref-counted channel per campaign, and I verified it with two browsers on production. I also added importing adventure notes from photos, and tested it on real pages. The cheaper model transcribed the prose fine but made four silent wrong values in three pages, table cells and a dice count, and never flagged one. The larger model made none, so vision uses that one, at roughly three times the cost per page. The provider's content filter also refuses to transcribe published book prose. I let that be a clear error and didn't try to prompt around it.

One experiment went nowhere, usefully. I tried an expert-offload inference engine on the older GPU, after freeing enough RAM to load it. It died during CUDA graph capture, because the Triton version it needs can't compile any atomic operation for that architecture. RAM was never the problem. I cleaned up the 33 GB image and its build cache and wrote down that it's a Volta-or-newer idea.

highlights.oneLiner: Found a stray lease made the proxy evict ComfyUI and hang it until timeout.
Renders hold the shared GPU through a lease; one bad client name froze it.
Added power counters to internal fleet monitoring; one box is 85% of draw.
Agent brain now loads fully into RAM; cold generation went 4.6 to 32 tok/s.
